newsitem.title: UK: "Creeping coup" talk hits Russia debt prices.
newsitem.headline: "Creeping coup" talk hits Russia debt prices.

text.p: Prices for Russian debt slumped on Thursday in a market shaken by the latest and very public Kremlin infighting and the general downturn in emerging debt, traders said.
"It's the politics and this Lebed coup business," one said.
On Wednesday, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accused security chief Alexander Lebed of preparing to seize power in a "creeping coup" while President Boris Yeltsin awaits heart surgery.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin this morning gave partial support to Kulikov but dismissed talk of coups or mutinies.

The price of Vneshekonomobank dollar debt, foreign commercial loans to the former Soviet Union which are in the process of being restructured, slumped three cents in the morning to just over 74 percent of face value.
That compares to a record high of almost 80 cents in the dollar earlier this month.
Russian Finance Ministry dollar bonds (MinFins) also dropped.
A trader at one European bank said the fall in prices was also due to weakness in the emerging debt market as a whole, which is seeing a correction after surging all year.
Investors were now taking the opportunity to cash in some of their profits, he added.
Prices of Russian debt have risen 150 percent since the start of this year and many analysts predicit further gains once the country issues its planned Eurobond, expected next month.
